articles.title: Preserve subtraction direction in a clinical change-score import
articles.excerpt: A CSV column named change hides a question: which number was subtracted from which? Consider two synthetic teaching records, both describing a score moving from 8 at baseline to 5 at week 12. One sour…
articles.body: A CSV column named change hides a question: which number was subtracted from which? Consider two synthetic teaching records , both describing a score moving from 8 at baseline to 5 at week 12. One source reports follow-up minus baseline: -3 . Another reports baseline minus follow-up: +3 . Loading those numbers into one unlabelled column creates an avoidable review problem. The sign is part of the source convention, not a standalone clinical interpretation. The Cochrane Handbook describes both subtraction directions for change scores in section 6.5.1. Section 6.5.2.1 discusses extracting final measurements and change scores.

articles.title: How to Pull Live Crypto Liquidations From 13 Exchange Feeds in Python
articles.excerpt: Liquidation data is one of those things that looks simple until you try to collect it yourself. Every derivatives venue publishes forced closes in its own format, over its own WebSocket, with its own…
articles.body: Liquidation data is one of those things that looks simple until you try to collect it yourself. Every derivatives venue publishes forced closes in its own format, over its own WebSocket, with its own throttling rules. Some send every print, some send at most one per contract per second, some only expose a delayed list. If you want a single number for "how much got liquidated in the last 24 hours, and on which side", you end up maintaining a dozen socket clients before you write a line of analysis. This post skips that part.

Fixer un budget, une durée et les informations bloquantes. Vérifier les livrables avant une action externe. Le fil de la série Sept repères pour déléguer du travail à une IA. articles.excerpt: A dam good moon.
articles.body: Get ready stargazers! The full "Beaver supermoon" rises in the eastern sky, offering up a spectacular display shortly after sunset tonight (Nov. 24). Here's what you need to know. November's full moon occurs at 9:53 a.m. EST (1453 GMT) on Nov. 24, as the lunar disk passes opposite the sun in our sky, making it appear fully lit from our perspective. The November full moon is often referred to as the Beaver Moon because it rises around the time the small mammals are hard at work building their lodges in preparation for the winter. The Beaver Moon is also set to be a dazzling supermoon , because it turns full as the natural satellite passes within 90% of perigee , when it is at its closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

articles.excerpt: Researchers have successfully grown potatoes in simulated lunar regolith, possibly opening the door for farming on future moon bases.
articles.body: It's no secret that NASA is working towards a permanent presence on the moon. The space agency even plans to build a moon base for its astronauts to call home. But humans living inside lunar habitats around the clock will need three square meals a day, so researchers have been working on how to grow food on the moon. To that end, a team from the College of Agricultural Sciences at Oregon State University have been raising potatoes in simulated moon dust with promising results. The researchers published their findings Nov. 20 in the Microgravity science journal.
